key_insight: A polymorphic high-entropy oxide photocatalyst, paired with microalgae as a sacrificial carbon-negative agent, dramatically improves solar-driven CO2 conversion to CO and CH4.
engineering_relevance: The work suggests a scalable catalyst-design and process-integration route for greener CO2 utilization by combining surface chemistry tuning with biological CO2 capture.
method: Design an AB2O6-type high-entropy oxide, (Cs1/7Ba4/7Bi2/7)(Nb1/2Ta1/2)2O6, with layered perovskite/pyrochlore bi-polymorphy.
Use Cs and Ba to raise surface basicity for CO2 chemisorption and Bi to promote polarization and charge separation.
Test photocatalytic CO2 reduction with and without sacrificial agents, including microalgae and microplastics, under solar-driven conditions.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that microalgae boosted CO and CH4 production by about 10-fold and 4-fold, respectively, relative to the HEO-only system.
watch_item: Practical deployment will depend on maintaining stable photocatalyst performance while managing microalgae handling, separation, and reaction-condition compatibility.
paper_title: Sustainable photocatalytic CO2 conversion using microalgae as a carbon-negative scavenger
